In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
trust in the Internet is the most influential target of trust in our study, followed by trust in the provider and trust in the IS.
trust in the IS is the most important target of trust in the context of information systems, but it is not sufficient to foster IS use on its own.

the trust in the provider has a positive direct and indirect effect on the intention to use the system, and the trust in the Internet has an indirect effect on the perceived usefulness, ease of use, perceived risk, intention to use the IS and the perceived trustworthiness of the IS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
trust is not only a matter of trust in the IS but that trust in the provider, the Internet and the IS are equally important in the context IS use.
IS research should not only focus on fostering trust in an IS itself but also consider the importance of multiple targets of trust.
IS researchers should focus more strongly on trust in the Internet and trust in the provider.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IS research should consider multiple targets of trust in order to understand IS use from a holistic point of view.
trust in IS use does not only depend on users’ trust in the system but also on their trust in other targets.
trust in an IS is not a standalone construct, but rather a construct that needs to be understood in the context of a network of other trust relationships.
